incoming_contract_bindings.literal_statement: Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with quantum characteristic $e$, and let $S^{\lambda}$ be the type-A Hecke Specht module of this page in the Dipper-James convention ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) for $\lambda\vdash n$. Then for all partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ the modules $S^{\lambda}$ and $S^{\mu}$ lie in the same block of $H_{F,q}(S_n)$ if and only if $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same $e$-core ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Equivalently the blocks of $H_{F,q}(S_n)$ are indexed by the $e$-cores $\gamma$ of size at most $n$ with $|\gamma|\equiv n\pmod e$, and the block of $S^{\lambda}$ is determined by $C_e(\lambda)$. (For $e=\infty$ the Hecke algebra is semisimple and each partition is its own core, so the statement is the trivial block decomposition.)

incoming_contract_bindings.literal_statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with FINITE quantum characteristic $e=e(F,q)$, $2\le e<\infty$, residue set $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ with representatives $0,1,\dots,e-1$ embedded in $F$, and the cyclic affine type-A Cartan datum with dominant weights $P^+$ and pairing $(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]], [[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). Fix $\Lambda\in P^+$ of level $\ell=\sum_{i\in I}(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$ and put $\lambda_i:=(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$.

**(NG) Nondegenerate case $q\ne1$.** The affine Hecke algebra of type $A_{d-1}$ at parameter $q$ is the unital $F$-algebra $H_d$ with generators $X_1^{\pm1},\dots,X_d^{\pm1}$, $T_1,\dots,T_{d-1}$ and relations (4.2)-(4.5) of the source: $X_rX_s=X_sX_r$, $X_rX_r^{-1}=1$, $T_rX_rT_r=qX_{r+1}$, $T_rX_s=X_sT_r$ ($s\notin\{r,r+1\}$), $T_r^2=(q-1)T_r+q$, $T_rT_{r+1}T_r=T_{r+1}T_rT_{r+1}$, $T_rT_s=T_sT_r$ ($|r-s|>1$). The **cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is $H^\Lambda_d:=H_d/\langle\prod_{i\in I}(X_1-q^i)^{\lambda_i}\rangle$.

**(DG) Degenerate case $q=1$** (then necessarily $\operatorname{char}F=e>0$). The **degenerate affine Hecke algebra** $H_d$ is the unital $F$-algebra with generators $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ and relations (3.2)-(3.5): $x_rx_s=x_sx_r$, $s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1$, $s_rx_s=x_ss_r$ ($s\notin\{r,r+1\}$), $s_r^2=1$, braid and distant commutation; its ordered monomials $x_1^{m_1}\cdots x_d^{m_d}w$ form an $F$-basis (the field-independent form of the presentation recorded in the source; the equivalent C-statement with its AC bookkeeping lives on the batch-17 page, which is outside this page's declared prerequisite closure and is deliberately not consumed here, see the batch notes). The **degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is $H^\Lambda_d:=H_d/\langle\prod_{i\in I}(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}\rangle$.

**Conventions.** $H^\Lambda_0=F$; the cyclotomic polynomial is imposed on the FIRST polynomial generator; $T_r$ acts on positions $r,r+1$. The Hecke parameter is the one of [[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] ($T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$). It is NOT the parameter of [[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]]: that page's generator satisfies $S^2=(Q-1)S+Q$ with $Q$ the square of its displayed parameter and $S=-q\,t$, so in the present normalisation it carries the parameter $Q$, not $q$; the two normalisations must be translated by the dictionary recorded there and are not identified here. At level one $\Lambda=\Lambda_j$, $H^\Lambda_d$ is the finite type-A Hecke algebra $H_{F,q}(S_d)$ if $q\ne1$ and the group algebra $FS_d$ if $q=1$ ([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]). Only finite $e$ is treated: the source's $e=0$ branches ($q$ not a root of unity, and the characteristic-zero degeneration, whose quiver is $A_\infty$) are outside this page's cyclic scope and are deferred in the batch notes. No choice principle is used.

incoming_contract_bindings.literal_statement:
Let R be a commutative ring, n≥0, ℓ≥1, and z,U_1,...,U_ℓ units of R. Define H_n by commuting invertible X_1,...,X_n, finite generators T_i satisfying (T_i−z)(T_i+1)=0, the type-A braid/distant relations, T_iX_iT_i=zX_(i+1), distant mixed commutation, and ∏_a(X_1−U_a)=0. For n=0 set H_0=R. The grading variable v is not z. An ℓ-multipartition λ of n is an ordered tuple of partitions; dominance compares every cumulative component/row sum. Fill tλ in component,row,column order. Put a_k=Σ_(b<k)|λ^(b)|, uλ=∏_k∏_(j≤a_k)(X_j−U_k), xλ=Σ_(w∈Sλ)T_w, mλ=xλuλ, Mλ=mλH_n. The row subgroup Sλ stabilizes the rows of tλ. The presentation involution * fixes all X_j,T_i and reverses products. For standard s,t of shapeλ put m_st=T_d(s)*mλT_d(t), where tλd(s)=s. Denote by H^{>λ} the span of higher Murphy shapes once their basis/cell law is established by [[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]], and Sλ the right cell/Specht module with basis m_t and action from that cell law. Its cellular form defines Dλ=Sλ/radSλ; Dλ may vanish.

Types are EXACTLY all ℓ-multipartitions of n, including empty components, not all multicompositions. A semistandard tableau S has labels (row,component) ordered by component then row, weak rows, strict columns, and a label of component a can occur only in physical component b≤a; its type counts each label with the multiplicity of that multipartition row. For a standard s, µ(s) replaces each entry by its row/component in tµ. Set m_(S,t)=Σ_(s:µ(s)=S)m_st and m_(S,T)=Σ_(s,t:µ(s)=S,ν(t)=T)m_st. Define M=⊕_(λ multipartition of n)Mλ and C_n=End_(H_n)(M), with ordinary composition. For S,T of shapeλ and typesµ,ν, the map φ_ST, once justified by [[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]], sends mαh to δ_(α,ν)m_(S,T)h. Its right cell module ∆λ has basis v_T for semistandard T of multipartition types, contravariant cell form and quotient Lλ. Let Tλ be the unique tableau of shape/typeλ, and let eλ be the identity projection onto Mλ. Put ω=(∅,...,∅,(1^n)) and e=eω; mω=1, so Mω=H_n. In particular H_n is an actual direct summand of M. Weight projections for Jantzen theory are eν with ν multipartition. Define K_(λ,ν)=#SStdν(λ). All asserted module/form/map laws are discharged by the linked local theorem/lemma suppliers; the definition itself does not claim their proofs or the primitive residue-content classification.

incoming_contract_bindings.literal_statement: Let $F$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital $F$-algebra with centre $Z(A):=\{z\in A:za=az	ext{ for all }a\in A\}$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). A **central idempotent** of $A$ is an idempotent $e\in Z(A)$; it is **primitive** when $e\ne0$ and $e$ is not the sum of two nonzero orthogonal central idempotents. Then $Z(A)$ is a finite-dimensional commutative $F$-algebra, so $1\in Z(A)$ admits a decomposition $$1=e_1+\cdots+e_k$$ into pairwise orthogonal primitive central idempotents ([[lem-the-identity-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-decomposes-into-primitive-central-idempotents]]), and this decomposition is unique up to order ([[lem-central-idempotent-decompositions-of-one-are-unique]]). A **block** of $A$ is the two-sided ideal $B=eA=Ae$ cut out by a primitive central idempotent $e$. The blocks are pairwise orthogonal two-sided ideals, $A=B_1\oplus\cdots\oplus B_k$ as $F$-algebras with units $e_i$, each $B_i$ is an indecomposable two-sided ideal, and for every (not necessarily finite-dimensional) $A$-module $M$ one has $M=\bigoplus_{i=1}^ke_iM$ as $A$-modules; a simple $A$-module $S$ satisfies $e_iS\ne0$ for exactly one $i$ and then $S=e_iS$ lies in the corresponding block. Nothing here asserts that a block is semisimple or simple, and the construction is choice-free.

incoming_contract_bindings.literal_statement: Let $e\ge2$ and $\lambda\vdash n$ with $\beta$-set $X$ ([[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]], hooks as in [[lem-hooks-are-bead-gap-pairs-on-an-abacus]]). $\lambda$ is an **$e$-core** when $e\notin H(\lambda)$, that is, when $\lambda$ has no hook of length $e$. For a $\beta$-set $X$ let $X^{(e)}_i=\{a\in\mathbb N_0:ae+i\in X\}$ be the set of row labels of the beads on runner $i$; set $X^{(e)}=\bigcup_{i=0}^{e-1}\{ae+i:0\le a\le|X^{(e)}_i|-1\}$ (the *top-packed* $\beta$-set) and define the **$e$-core** $C_e(\lambda):=P(X^{(e)})$. Choose the $\beta$-set so that $|X|\equiv0\pmod e$, and define the **$e$-quotient** $Q_e(\lambda)=(\lambda^{(0)},\dots,\lambda^{(e-1)})$ by $\lambda^{(i)}=P(X^{(e)}_i)$ and the **$e$-weight** by $w_e(\lambda):=|Q_e(\lambda)|=\sum_i|\lambda^{(i)}|$. Every $e$-core is $e$-regular and $e$-restricted. The definitions are independent of the chosen $\beta$-set: shifting by $1$ permutes the runners and changes the quotient only by a cyclic shift of the components, which the normalisation $|X|\equiv0\pmod e$ removes (proved below in the core-independence theorem of this page).

incoming_contract_bindings.literal_statement: Over any field $F$, use the defining relations of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], writing $q_H$ for the nondegenerate Hecke parameter. For a monic degree-$\ell>0$ cyclotomic polynomial $f$, with nonzero constant term in the nondegenerate branch, the quotient by $f(X_1)=0$ is spanned by $X_1^{a_1}\cdots X_d^{a_d}T_w$, and the degenerate quotient by $f(x_1)=0$ is spanned by $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_d^{a_d}w$, where $0\le a_r<\ell$ and $w\in S_d$. In particular each quotient has dimension at most $\ell^d d!$. This applies to $f(t)=\prod_{i\in I}(t-q_H^i)^{\lambda_i}$ and $f(t)=\prod_{i\in I}(t-i)^{\lambda_i}$ in the two finite-quantum-characteristic branches, with $\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i$. No independence or separate relation $f(X_r)=0$ or $f(x_r)=0$ for $r>1$ is asserted. If $\ell=0,d>0$, the relation $1=0$ gives the zero algebra with empty spanning family; for $d=0$ the algebra is $F$ with singleton empty monomial.

Two cell modules share a block exactly when they are linked by a finite chain of cell modules whose neighboring terms share a simple factor. For one primitive idempotent eµ per simple, dim eµAeν=Σλ[Cλ:Dµ][Cλ:Dν].

incoming_contract_bindings.literal_statement: Let $e\ge2$ and $\lambda\vdash n$ with $e$-core $C_e(\lambda)$ and $e$-weight $w_e(\lambda)=|Q_e(\lambda)|$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Then $n=|\lambda|=|C_e(\lambda)|+e\,w_e(\lambda)$, so $w_e(\lambda)=(n-|C_e(\lambda)|)/e\in\mathbb N_0$. Equivalently every sequence of rim $e$-hook removals from $\lambda$ down to its $e$-core ([[thm-e-core-is-independent-of-the-rim-hook-removal-order]]) has exactly $w_e(\lambda)$ steps, and $w_e(\lambda)=|Q_e(\lambda)|$ equals both the number of hooks of the multipartition $Q_e(\lambda)$ and, by the bijection of [[thm-e-quotient-controls-hooks-divisible-by-e]], the number of hooks of $\lambda$ of length divisible by $e$.

incoming_contract_bindings.literal_statement:
Let F be any field, q_H in F^× have finite multiplicative order e>=2, ell>=1 be arbitrary, and Q_a=q_H^(c_a), with charges c_a in Z. Fix n>=0 and let S_F be the cyclotomic q-Schur algebra with summands indexed by all ell-multipartitions of n. Put

$$O=F[t,t^{-1}]_{(t-1)},\quad \pi=t-1,\quad K=F(t),\quad z=q_Ht,\quad U_a=Q_at^{na}.$$

Let Delta_O(lambda) be its standard Weyl lattice with its actual cellular form. Define

$$\Delta_O(\lambda)(s)=\{v:\langle v,\Delta_O(\lambda)\rangle\subseteq\pi^sO\},\qquad\Delta_F(\lambda)^s=(\Delta_O(\lambda)(s)+\pi\Delta_O(\lambda))/\pi\Delta_O(\lambda).$$

Then this is a filtration by S_F-submodules, its first term is rad Delta_F(lambda), it terminates, and in the INTEGER Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional S_F-modules,

$$\sum_{s>0}[\Delta_F(\lambda)^s]=\sum_{\mu}J_{\lambda\mu}[\Delta_F(\mu)].$$

For a node x=(i,j,a), define the rim hook r_x^lambda and foot f_x^lambda=(lambda'_j,j,a) as in LM, leg(r_x^lambda)=lambda'_j-i, and res_O(i,j,a)=U_a z^(j-i). If lambda strictly dominates mu, set

$$J_{\lambda\mu}=\sum_{\substack{x\in[\lambda],\ y\in[\mu]\\[\lambda]\setminus r_x^\lambda=[\mu]\setminus r_y^\mu}}(-1)^{\operatorname{leg}(r_x^\lambda)+\operatorname{leg}(r_y^\mu)}\nu_\pi\big(\operatorname{res}_O(f_x^\lambda)-\operatorname{res}_O(f_y^\mu)\big);$$

otherwise set J_(lambda mu)=0. Equal remainder diagrams force equal hook lengths. Every displayed difference is nonzero in K, including samecomponent terms with distinct labels, by the local foot-exponent separation proof. No level-one or characteristic-zero restriction is present.

Its standard classes form a Z-basis of G_0 and weight dimensions dim ∆λeν=K_(λ,ν) give a unitriangular multipartition Kostka matrix. Over the universal ring/DVR the standards and forms are free and eν*=eν. The exact corner functor V↦Veω gives ∆λeω≅Sλ and Lλeω≅Dλ (possibly0), so [∆λ:Lµ]=[Sλ:Dµ] for Dµ≠0. The centers Z(C_n) and Z(H_n) are canonically isomorphic because Mω=H_n is a summand, and ∆λ,∆µ share a C_n-block iff Sλ,Sµ share an H_n-block. Standard/Specht linkage is exactly shared-simple-factor linkage. No equality-of-residue-contents ⇒ primitive-block assertion is included.

incoming_contract_bindings.literal_statement: Let $e\ge2$ and $\lambda\vdash n$. The top-packed $\beta$-set $X^{(e)}$ of [[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]] does not depend on the chosen $\beta$-set of $\lambda$ up to a shift that leaves $P$ unchanged, so the $e$-core $C_e(\lambda)$ is a well-defined $e$-core partition; it is exactly the terminal partition reached by successively removing rim $e$-hooks (removable border strips of size $e$, [[def-removable-border-strip-and-height]], [[lem-hooks-correspond-to-removable-border-strips]]) until none is left. In particular every removal order gives the same terminal partition $C_e(\lambda)$, each removed strip has size exactly $e$, and the terminal partition contains no hook of length $e$.
